title: The Glory of God and the Sun of Righteousness
english: wickedness and the impiety joined to it

To sing: for God says the Son glorifies the Father and the slave fears his lord; and if I say, 'I am lord,' where is my fear? and if I say, 'I am father,' where is my glory? (Ps 112:3,4). Perhaps also regarding the sun of righteousness, if it is in some rises according to which it rises. These have a relationship (or are themselves) to the rises in which paradise is planted. If they have a harmony in these rises, it is fitting to praise the name of the Lord according to the rises by which it rises and the settings. For he was able for Israel, but he rose for the believing nations. Since not with unwise and unjust judgment he was able to rise for those also, having received providence's judgments everywhere and all things from the Lord: Praise his name; the Lord is high above all nations, his glory is above the heavens.

And the words being taken more simply declare that as God of all things he provides, being high above all nations as a king, and having his glory in the heavens ruling also the rational ranks there. But with a deeper mind, the Lord is high above all believing nations, being praised by them with pure life, practical and contemplative life. And upon the heavens, which no longer bear the image of the swine but the heavenly, his glory reaches, just as he announces it to his own disciples: for the heavens declare the glory of God (Ps 19:1). For certainly some declare it. If you are able to say the glory of the Lord, the radiance of his glory, the Lord and our savior, you would follow what was said to the one being illuminated: And the glory of God has shone upon you (Lk 1:79).

And through the coming words, foreseeing the God of all, we learn, regarding how incomparably the Holy One is compared to all created things, he says: Who is like the Lord our God? (Ps 112:5-9). For there is no one like him, since he is alone.
